name: create_case
description: Create a new canonical service request. Wraps business_process.create_case — the connector performs no validation or business logic of its own beyond required-field presence.

request_schema.title: string, required
request_schema.requestor: string, required — role/team identifier, never a named individual

example_request.title: Shared workstation will not power on
example_request.description: Ward reception shared workstation does not power on after a scheduled restart.

case.title: Shared workstation will not power on
case.description: Ward reception shared workstation does not power on after a scheduled restart.

history.detail: Case submitted in category 'Digital Support' with priority 'Medium'

caveat: Not idempotent by itself — the calling flow is responsible for de-duplicating retried submissions before calling this operation (see power_platform/README.md failure architecture).

name: transition_case
description: Move a case to a new lifecycle stage. Wraps business_process.transition_case, which itself calls validate_transition — the connector never decides whether a move is legal.

response_schema.case: object — canonical Case after the move (on success)
response_schema.error: string — exception type name (on failure, e.g. InvalidLifecycleTransitionError)

case.title: Rostering application intermittent timeout
case.description: Line-of-business rostering application intermittently times out when generating weekly rota exports.

history.detail: Case submitted in category 'Application Support' with priority 'Medium'

caveat: Idempotent in effect, not by mechanism: replaying the same move once it has already happened raises InvalidLifecycleTransitionError rather than silently succeeding twice — e.g. {'error': 'InvalidLifecycleTransitionError', 'detail': "Invalid case lifecycle transition: 'Routed' -> 'Resolved'"}. Callers should treat that specific error as 'already applied', not a failure.

name: get_case
description: Retrieve current canonical case state by case_id.

case.title: Laptop will not connect to corporate Wi-Fi
case.description: Staff laptop repeatedly fails to authenticate against the corporate wireless network after a recent OS update.
case.resolution_notes: Reissued network profile; laptop reconnected successfully.

history.detail: Case submitted in category 'Digital Support' with priority 'Medium'

caveat: No persistence layer exists yet (see business_process/README.md) — business_process holds no case store to read from. This contract is defined now so Power Platform integration design is not blocked on it, but it cannot be backed by real data until a persistence milestone lands. The example response is drawn from a synthetic fixture, not a live read.

name: evaluate_sla
description: Evaluate a case's current SLA status. Wraps business_process.sla.get_sla_target + evaluate_sla — the connector performs no breach-threshold maths itself.

name: evaluate_escalation
description: Determine whether a case currently qualifies for escalation, and why. Wraps business_process.should_escalate / determine_escalation_reason.

response_schema.reason: string or null — one of EscalationReason

name: resolve_case
description: Resolve a case with an outcome and notes. Wraps business_process.resolve_case.

example_request.notes: Restarted the affected service; timeout no longer reproduces.

case.title: Rostering application intermittent timeout
case.description: Line-of-business rostering application intermittently times out when generating weekly rota exports.
case.resolution_notes: Restarted the affected service; timeout no longer reproduces.

history.detail: Case submitted in category 'Application Support' with priority 'Medium'

caveat: Idempotent via the same mechanism as transition_case — a repeat call once already resolved raises InvalidLifecycleTransitionError.

name: list_service_categories
description: List the canonical service taxonomy. A static read over business_process.taxonomy.ServiceCategory — no decision involved.

name: retrieve_queue_assignment
description: Given a service category, return the canonical queue and default owning team it routes to. Wraps business_process.route_category + assign_owner — the connector does not decide routing itself.
caveat: Returns the canonical Queue value, not a platform-specific display name — a caller that needs the Dynamics queue name should separately use the dynamics365 adapter (see docs/crm_schema_mapping.md).

name: sync_dynamics_representation
description: Push the current canonical case's Dynamics reference representation to the CRM boundary. Wraps dynamics365.to_dynamics_incident for translation; the actual CRM write is a future, live-connector concern — see integrations/README.md. Added beyond the 8 canonical-facing operations because both the intake and resolution-notification flows need a distinct step for 'persist the translated representation', which is CRM-facing rather than canonical-facing.

incident.title: Laptop will not connect to corporate Wi-Fi
incident.description: Staff laptop repeatedly fails to authenticate against the corporate wireless network after a recent OS update.

resolution.subject: Fixed
resolution.description: Reissued network profile; laptop reconnected successfully.

caveat: No live Dataverse write occurs — 'upserted' here describes the intended real behaviour (keyed on ticketnumber, see docs/crm_schema_mapping.md Idempotency and external IDs), not an actual CRM call.
